assumptions: The base is fixed and the links are rigid. This model uses nominal manufacturer geometry, not calibration of a particular lab arm.
The upright mug pose is supplied exactly. Perception does not estimate it in this lesson.
G is the manufacturer's hand TCP between the fingers. The current pose is computed from q.
G* is a chosen grasp target at the mug center, with its z axis pointing down and x axis following the mug handle direction.
The approach target is 0.10 m behind G* along its local z axis. Its position is therefore 0.10 m above G* in world z.
The targets are pose requests. This lesson performs no IK, collision check, contact simulation, grasp-stability test, or hardware execution.
Official collision shapes are used as low-detail visual geometry. Fingers are held symmetrically open.
